title: heap-buffer-overflow in pycore_interpframe.h _PyFrame_Initialize
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 184-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached, then neither completed nor faulted

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3f8e2e6fec in _PyEvalFramePushAndInit; by function: _PyEvalFramePushAndInit is where host ASan reported the access

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) at si_addr=0x69c7ca, re-measured 2026-10-19 with ONLY=09 bash probe/run-cheribsd.sh because the 2026-10-06 cheri11 run kept no fault site. 0x69c7ca is not a heap address on this guest (its heap is around 0x40a00000-0x40be0000), so the faulting access went through a small integer held where a capability belonged -- the same fingerprint as case 01's address=0x7 and case 10's address=0x10. The defective store succeeded and the fault is downstream of it. WITHDRAWN.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=24 (spatial-20261006-105111); sublet DETECTED cause=24 (sublet-20261006-112658); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=2 (cheri11)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-buffer-overflow (WRITE 8) at _PyFrame_Initialize Include/internal/pycore_frame.h:150 | _PyEvalFramePushAndInit Python/ceval.c:1724. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
note: (2) is a genuine detection: cause=28 on `stc zero, 0x0(a3)`, the defective store itself. The defect is Include/internal/pycore_frame.h:150, `frame->localsplus[i] = NULL;` in a loop bounded by code->co_nlocalsplus while the frame was sized by code->co_framesize -- the two disagree, so the NULL stores run past the frame. (1) is NO-READING, not a miss: the trigger reached its mark and then neither completed nor faulted, including on a re-run at --timeout 900. (3) WITHDRAWN. si_code=2 PROT_CHERI_TAG at si_addr=0x69c7ca, which is not a heap address, so what faulted was a dereference of a small integer sitting where a capability belonged, not the bounds check. An earlier draft of this review guessed the untagged value was a NULL the overflow had stored over a neighbour's capability; the measured si_addr is 0x69c7ca, not 0, so that guess is withdrawn -- the overflow corrupted a field and a later load of it was dereferenced. See cheribsd_why_allowed for why the store was allowed on that arm, and note that an 8-byte overshoot is far too small for the representability rule that restored case 08.
cheribsd_why_allowed: CheriBSD runs pymalloc too -- that build has WITH_PYMALLOC 1 and probe/run-cheribsd.sh sets no PYTHONMALLOC -- so on a NESTED case the object is a pymalloc block inside an arena there as well, and CheriBSD's malloc bounds the arena. That, not size-class rounding, is why the defective access succeeds on this arm; rounding is a second and much smaller effect that only matters where the object is malloc's own. Measured 2026-10-19 with tools/cheribsd/capbounds, the rounding at the sizes this corpus allocates is 16->16, 24->32, 48->48, 97->112, 100->112, 184->192, 200->224, 216->224, 400->448, 512->512, 8193->10240, 524321->655360. The 8-byte overshoot here is also three orders of magnitude too small for the representability rule that restored case 08 (a small block keeps its tag out to +16384), so si_code=2 cannot be the bounds rule arriving under the tag code. The access succeeded and the fault is downstream.
